title: Math Blitz: Speed Challenge
description: Think fast, calculate faster! 25 rapid-fire math questions covering mental arithmetic, algebra, geometry, number patterns, probability, and real-world problem solving. From cricket batting averages to train journey calculations, put your mathematical brain to the ultimate speed test!
learning_objectives: Strengthen mental arithmetic skills with percentages, fractions, and ratios
Build confidence in solving algebraic equations and evaluating expressions quickly
Apply geometry concepts like area, perimeter, angles, and the Pythagorean theorem
Recognize and extend number patterns and sequences
Solve real-world word problems involving money, distance, time, and probability
Develop speed and accuracy in mathematical reasoning under time pressure

how_to_play.title: How to Play
steps: Read each math question carefully -- many are set in real-world Indian contexts like cricket, shopping, train journeys, and cooking
Select your answer before the 20-second timer runs out
Earn 10 points per correct answer, plus streak bonuses of 5 points for consecutive correct answers
Work through all 25 questions covering arithmetic, algebra, geometry, patterns, probability, and word problems
Questions get progressively harder -- start strong and build momentum for the tougher ones at the end
tips: For percentage problems, remember that 10% is just dividing by 10 -- use this as a building block for other percentages
In algebra, substitute the answer options back into the equation if solving feels slow -- back-calculation saves time
For geometry questions, visualise the shape and recall key formulas: area of triangle = 1/2 x base x height, area of circle = pi x r squared
Build answer streaks for maximum points -- if you are unsure, eliminate obviously wrong options first
For speed-distance-time problems, remember: Speed = Distance / Time, and keep units consistent

questions.question: Ananya buys a notebook marked at Rs 80 and gets a 10% discount. How much does she pay?
Rohit scored 45, 62, 38, and 55 runs in 4 cricket innings. What is his average score per innings?
A recipe for 4 servings of dal requires 3/4 cup of masoor dal. Priya wants to cook for 8 people. How many cups of masoor dal does she need?
In a class of 40 students, the ratio of boys to girls is 3:5. How many girls are there in the class?
What is 3/8 expressed as a percentage?
Solve for x: 2x + 7 = 19
What are the next two numbers in this sequence? 2, 6, 18, 54, __, __
A rectangular cricket pitch is 20 metres long and 3 metres wide. What is its perimeter?
Kiran has a bag containing 3 red balls, 5 blue balls, and 2 green balls. If she picks one ball at random, what is the probability of picking a blue ball?
A shopkeeper in Chandni Chowk buys a shawl for Rs 400 and sells it for Rs 500. What is his profit percentage?
The Rajdhani Express covers 1,380 km from Delhi to Kolkata in 12 hours. What is its average speed in km/h?
If the value of the expression 3a - 2b is 13 when a = 5, what is the value of b?
A circular rangoli design has a radius of 7 cm. What is its area? (Use pi = 22/7)
Arjun walks 6 km north, then 8 km east. What is the shortest straight-line distance from his starting point to his current position?
What is the next number in this pattern? 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, __
During a Diwali sale, a TV originally priced at Rs 30,000 is offered at a 15% discount. But there is an additional 10% discount on the reduced price. What is the final price?
Two trains start from Delhi and Jaipur (280 km apart) at the same time, heading towards each other. Train A moves at 60 km/h and Train B at 80 km/h. After how many hours will they meet?
In a cricket tournament, a batsman's strike rate is calculated as (Runs scored / Balls faced) x 100. If Virat scored 72 runs off 48 balls, what is his strike rate?
The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2:3:4. What is the measure of the largest angle?
A two-digit number has its digits summing to 9. If the digits are reversed, the new number is 27 more than the original. What is the original number?
A cylindrical water tank in a village has a radius of 3.5 metres and a height of 4 metres. What is its capacity in cubic metres? (Use pi = 22/7)
Sneha invests Rs 12,000 at 8% simple interest per annum. After how many years will her total amount become Rs 16,800?
Two dice are thrown simultaneously. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers on the two dice is 7?
If 3^(2x-1) = 27, what is the value of x?
A train 150 metres long passes a man standing on a platform in 10 seconds. It then passes the entire platform (which is 350 metres long) in how many seconds?

glossary_terms.definition: A way of expressing a number as a fraction of 100. For example, 25% means 25 out of 100. To find a percentage of a number, multiply the number by the percentage and divide by 100. Percentages are widely used in discounts, interest rates, exam scores, and cricket statistics.

A comparison of two or more quantities expressed in the form a:b. For example, a ratio of 3:5 means for every 3 parts of the first quantity, there are 5 parts of the second. Ratios are used in recipes, map scales, mixing paints, and dividing quantities.

In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse (the longest side, opposite the right angle) is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides. Expressed as a^2 + b^2 = c^2, where c is the hypotenuse. This theorem is used extensively in distance calculations, construction, and navigation.

In cricket, the strike rate of a batsman is calculated as (Total Runs Scored / Total Balls Faced) x 100. A strike rate of 150 means the batsman scores 150 runs for every 100 balls faced, indicating aggressive batting. In bowling, strike rate refers to the number of balls bowled per wicket taken.

Interest calculated only on the original principal amount. The formula is SI = (P x R x T) / 100, where P is the principal, R is the rate of interest per annum, and T is the time in years. Unlike compound interest, simple interest does not add earned interest back to the principal.

A measure of how likely an event is to occur, expressed as a number between 0 (impossible) and 1 (certain). Calculated as the number of favourable outcomes divided by the total number of possible outcomes. For example, the probability of rolling a 3 on a fair die is 1/6.

achievements.title: Math Starter
achievements.description: Score at least 100 points by answering 10 or more questions correctly -- you have solid math foundations!

achievements.title: Speed Solver
achievements.description: Score at least 180 points by answering 18 or more questions correctly with streak bonuses -- your mental math is impressive!

achievements.title: Math Wizard
achievements.description: Achieve a streak of 7 or more consecutive correct answers -- your mathematical instincts are razor sharp!

transfer_exercises.real_world: Making fast calls during a team project deadline crunch
transfer_exercises.challenge: Practice making a decision in under 60 seconds on something you've been procrastinating. Reflect on the outcome.

transfer_exercises.game_context: Recovering from mistakes in rapid gameplay
transfer_exercises.real_world: Bouncing back after a failed presentation or test

coaching_moment: The skills you're building today compound over time. Accuracy matters more than speed — a small delay for correctness pays big dividends later.
cultural_context: Mathematics and logical reasoning are core subjects in India's JEE, NEET, and competitive examination landscape. Math Blitz: Speed Challenge develops the pattern recognition and analytical thinking that accelerates performance across these high-stakes assessments.
